text:
Miguel R.: quick q — we need a concrete proposal for OTEL keys for LLM requests. want something stable for dashboards + exporters. thoughts?

Anna K.: yes. current chaos: some folks use `model.name`, others `model` or `model_version`. we should standardize.

Priya S.: +1. also need to decide which things are span attrs vs resource attrs vs metrics. tokens are high-cardinality if we include breakdowns.

Tom B.: proposal sketch: resource attrs = deployment-level info (region, cluster_id, dedicated vs hosted), span attrs = per-request (model.family, model.revision, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cache_hit).

Miguel R.: can you paste a concrete attr list? PR wants strings we can paste into telemetry docs.

Tom B.: sure — rough:```
resource: 
  redwood.region: string
  redwood.env: string
  redwood.cluster_id: string
span: 
  redwood.llm.model.family: string  # e.g. gpt4o, llama2
  redwood.llm.model.full_name: string # full model id e.g. llama2-70b-chat-q8
  redwood.llm.model.revision: string # hashed/semver if available
  redwood.llm.quantized: bool
  redwood.llm.request.type: string # text, chat, embed, rerank
  redwood.llm.tokens.prompt: int
  redwood.llm.tokens.completion: int
  redwood.llm.tokens.total: int
  redwood.llm.cache.kv_hits: int
  redwood.llm.cache.kv_hit_ratio: double
  redwood.llm.routing.policy: string # latency|cost|region|fallback
  redwood.llm.billing.customer_tier: string
  redwood.llm.response.truncated: bool
```

Priya S.: I like the separation. Couple notes: 1) `full_name` could be high-cardinality if we include commit hashes; prefer stable release tags. 2) tokens as ints on spans — they inflate span size, but we need them for per-request cost accounting. agreeable?

Anna K.: on (1) — enforce `model.full_name` to be normalized: `{family}-{size}-{profile}` and keep `revision` separate for build hashes. that way dashboards group nicely.

Miguel R.: what about sampling? we can't export every span with token counts to cold storage, costs explode.

EVA L.: observability-bot suggests: sample 100% for last N seconds, then tail-sample by token count buckets for retention. maybe keep high-token requests at higher retention.

observability-bot: automated note: see retention tiers doc https://internal.redwood/telemetry/retention for policy templates. :gear:

Tom B.: technical detail: use numeric token attrs on span but also emit an aggregated metric `redwood.llm.tokens.processed` as a counter per model.family so long-term metrics don't need scanning traces.

Priya S.: yes metrics solve analytics. For dashboards that join traces->metrics we can link via `trace_id`. but metric cardinality must be limited: model.family only, not full_name.

Miguel R.: cache attrs — should we expose per-layer counts? (kv cache vs prefix cache)

Anna K.: keep two fields: `redwood.llm.cache.layer` (enum kv|prefix|none) and `redwood.llm.cache.hits` (int). Also `redwood.llm.cache.kv_hit_ratio` as double to compute percent. avoid exposing keys or prefixes.

Tom B.: note: prefix cache can be noisy because short prompts hit often. we should cap attr sizes and avoid arrays. single ints only.

Priya S.: security check — do any of these attrs leak PII? tokens counts are safe, model names are fine, but watch `routing.policy` if it encodes customer ids. use `customer_tier` not raw customer name.

Miguel R.: exporters — do we want these attrs in OTLP payload to datadog/newrelic? Some downstreams charge by span size.

EVA L.: recommendation: send full span attrs to internal long-term tracing (tempo/jaeger) for sampled traces. For SaaS exporters, send a minimized set (model.family, tokens.total bucketed, cache.hit bool, routing.policy) to control egress costs.

Anna K.: +1. define an "export profile" header we set at span creation: `redwood.telemetry.profile = "full" | "lite"`. exporter agents will drop heavy fields for `lite`.

Tom B.: implementation detail: add a preprocessor in collector pipeline that maps `redwood.llm.tokens.total` into buckets `0-64,65-512,513-2048,>2048` for lite exporters. store raw int only in internal store.

Priya S.: about naming: prefer `redwood.llm.*` namespace over `llm.*` to avoid collision. keep kebab/period style consistent. periods are ok for OTEL.

Miguel R.: anyone object to these keys? if not I'll open a PR in `telemetry-conventions.md` and a follow-up for collector config.

Anna K.: small nit: `redwood.llm.request.type` should have canonical values and we should document them (chat, text_generation, embedding, rerank). I'll add a table in the doc.

Priya S.: action: I'll prototype a collector pipeline that does export profiles + token bucketing. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Tom B.: I'll add the model normalization helper to the model onboarding CLI so `full_name` gets normalized.

Miguel R.: perfect. last thing — retention: recommend 30d full traces for P0 routes, 7d for normal, aggregated metrics kept 90d. agreeable?

EVA L.: observability-bot note: default retention templates applied: P0=30d, P1=14d, P2=7d. we can special-case token-buckets longer if needed.

Anna K.: sounds good. Miguel — tag me on the PR, I'll review naming and docs. :+1:

Miguel R.: thanks all. I'll draft the PR with the attr table and the collector snippets.

observability-bot: reminder scheduled — telemetry sync on Monday 10:00 to finalize conventions.

Tom B.: one last thought: add `redwood.llm.fallback.used` bool when routing falls back to cheaper model so we can track quality regressions.

Priya S.: good call. add `redwood.llm.routing.fallback_reason` limited enum (quota|latency|capacity) — keep short.

Miguel R.: ok that wraps it. PR incoming.
